taxonomic_note: Accepted and Texas-native at the state level. The project currently has only Mason County locked inside the target zone; broad ecoregion or horticultural presence is not converted into county proof.
look_here_first: Start with the classic bee-balm head: an aromatic perennial with opposite leaves and a dense rounded terminal head of pale lavender to pink bilabiate flowers rather than the tiered bracted whorls typical of M. citriodora and M. punctata.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Mason is the exact project target-zone county recovered from USDA-derived county distribution in the latest review. Broader Blackland/Cross Timbers and Texas native context is retained only as regional support.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the one-county HOLD.

best_field_traits: pale lavender to pink bilabiate corollas
flowering head not arranged as the strongly separated stacked whorls typical of M. citriodora
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with M. citriodora and M. punctata, wild bergamot usually presents a more conventional dense terminal head rather than conspicuous tiered whorls with showy bracts. Do not rely on flower color alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Rounded terminal bee-balm head and lack of the long-bristled citriodora bracts or heavily spotted yellow punctata corollas.

diagnostic_image_needs: direct comparison with M. citriodora and M. punctata
